tasks.title: Retire donor Minecraft instances after owner confirms migration
tasks.notes:
Problem: migration to ~/Projects/minecraft-mcp was completed on 2026-10-28 (#177), but donor instances and launcher profiles remain. This is owner-machine maintenance, not a tool capability change. Elapsed days alone do not establish successful use or authorize deletion.
Scope: Southampton Refine/instance, Minecraft Magic/instance, launcher profiles southampton-refine and fabric-loader-26.2, and Minecraft Magic/README.md. Plan: docs/plans/shared-minecraft-instance.md.
Acceptance: before removal, confirm successful standalone-instance use, inventory remaining saves, verify the recorded backups under ~/Projects/minecraft-save-backups/2026-10-28/, and obtain the owner's explicit decision on the scratch save New World (the plan requires this). Confirm Magic has no other save worth keeping. Retain backups and the relocated private sealed answers at ~/.local/share/ai-worldbuilder/bakeoff-sealed/truth.json; do not display their contents. Remove only the agreed donor folders/profiles and update the Magic README. Do not execute any of these actions as part of backlog refinement.
Verification: read-only inventory before removal; afterward check the agreed profiles/paths and that the standalone instance still references its intended saves. No tool unit test needed.

tasks.title: Identify the running save and its matching world checkout without loading providers
tasks.notes:
Problem: the redo workflow needs to choose --world before invoking a place-aware CLI; trying each checkout can trigger unrelated missing-provider failures. Those diagnostics are now separated into #227.
Scope: a read-only scripts/which_world.py discovery command that reads worlds/*/config/world.json and matches resolved save paths to the running MCP world's save. It must work without an already selected world and without importing world-owned providers. Reuse active_world.resolve_save and investigate the existing site_kit.mcp_reported_gameworld helper; that helper currently combines MCP reachability with session.lock file existence, which is not proof that a save is open. First establish what reliable identity the current bridge/runtime exposes; do not assume server status returns a save path or treat a stale lock file as evidence.
Acceptance: one verified matching checkout returns its name and resolved save path with exit 0; server unavailable, unknown identity, unmatched save, duplicate checkout matches or ambiguous running saves return nonzero with a clear reason and no guessed world. Resolve relative save paths against each checkout. Discovery never silently selects a default or weakens required --world on mutating commands. Add the command to AGENTS.md Start and redo Locate.
Verification: synthetic configs and mocked server/lock evidence cover unique match, duplicate names in different instance roots, relative paths, stale locks, malformed configs, unknown identity and server down. No live-world mutation. If authoritative identity is unavailable, record that limitation before choosing a fallback.

tasks.title: Explain layer exclusions and reconcile plan, write and readback counts
tasks.notes:
Problem: layer output is uneven: trees already writes a plan JSON but truncates console skip details; decor prints per-item rows; ground already aggregates skip reasons. A reported decor count difference (2582 versus 2533) is an observation, not yet evidence of lost writes.
Scope: lib/layers/{trees_layer,decor_layer,ground_layer}.py and the existing site_kit apply/result path as needed. First trace which stages those counts measure. Distinguish candidate items, accepted placements, final guarded plan positions, positions already correct, journal write positions and positions verified. Existing readback covers plan.cells; a smaller write count can be legitimate. Never infer a short write merely by subtracting unlike counts.
Acceptance: concise console counts by exclusion reason, including hedge above-lidar-ground warnings; full per-item reasons in an existing or extended world-local verification artifact, whose path is printed. Preserve existing review images/JSON consumers. Every count difference between planning, journal writes and readback is explained by the stage's semantics; unexplained loss or readback mismatch exits nonzero and cannot report success. Empty/no-change plans remain explicit and retain each layer's existing completion rules.
Verification: synthetic cases for already-correct blocks, intentional exclusions, truncated console/full artifact, empty decor, a legitimate plan/write difference and a simulated missing write. Extend existing layer/site_kit tests using MemoryBlocks or mocks; no live apply. Keep planning-policy changes such as #226 out of this task.

tasks.title: Run a checked layer redo with one lock and explicit partial-failure reporting
tasks.notes:
Problem: manual layer redo repeats world selection, undo ordering, lock handling, viewing and readback checks. A wrapper must preserve current journal/ownership semantics rather than create a second recovery system.
Interface: scripts/redo_layer.py --world W --cell tx,tz --layers trees,decor; dry run by default, --apply for live mutation. Validate layer names and combinations before any write; use canonical ground -> trees -> decor execution order. Reuse the existing layer, mask undo and site_lock paths. Background execution belongs to the caller; keep useful streamed progress and a final exit status, with no detached child left holding the lock.
Acceptance: preflight world identity, evidence/readiness and relevant masks before destructive steps; claim one lock for the entire live sequence and release on failure/interrupt. Trees redo clears decor before trees when required, reapplies only requested layers, and explicitly reports decor still undone if omitted. Ground-only redo preserves tree/decor masks, ownership and completion per #217; never clears them implicitly. Preview the intended operation sequence without writes, then re-plan/validate each apply against the state after required undos. Do not promise a pre-undo plan is identical to a post-undo plan.
For player-standing redo, check the selected player's hover move/view before mutation and re-establish it after apply; propagate movement failures instead of piping them away. Report no-player behaviour explicitly. On mask conflict, readback mismatch, failure or interrupt, stop further stages, return nonzero and report completed/undone/pending stages plus the existing site_recover/reconcile route. Do not automatically retry, use --skip-changed or claim transactional rollback. Success/cue only after every requested stage succeeds; sound cue failure cannot turn a landed build into a failed apply.
Verification: mocked orchestration with no live world: invalid input/no mutation, undo/apply ordering, ground preservation, trees-only leaves decor pending, missing masks, lock refusal/release, hover failure, interrupt and later-stage failure. Existing layer tests remain the source for placement correctness. Owner decision 2026-10-31 (#221, resolved): viewing belongs to redo; direct trees/decor/ground applies remain independent of player position. Implement checked viewing in the redo workflow only. #222 improves reporting but is not a mandatory implementation dependency.

tasks.title: Replace manual layer redo recipes with the checked wrapper
tasks.notes:
Problem: once #223 exists, parallel manual recipes in .claude/skills/redo/SKILL.md would drift from executable behaviour.
Scope: docs only. After #219 and #223, trees/decor/ground branches become locate, inspect the wrapper dry run, then run its explicit --apply under the documented lock/background contract. Keep feature redesign separate and retain the meaning of redo versus reapply established by #225 when available; do not make #225 a prerequisite for layer docs.
Acceptance: examples match the wrapper's actual parser; world selection, layer ordering, cleared-but-not-requested layers, ground preservation (#217), hover behaviour, nonzero exit and recovery messages are described once. No nested lock acquisition and no implication that background launch means completion. Remove superseded manual sequences rather than keeping two authoritative paths.
Verification: review examples against #223 CLI help and its orchestration tests; no live apply or prose-only unit tests.

tasks.title: Record feature builder provenance and support an explicit reapply workflow
tasks.notes:
Problem: redo_here.describe() only searches build_*.py for NAME; feature_build.run() reads the supplied path relative to cwd and calls apply without builder metadata. Therefore a journal entry cannot currently be assumed to contain a replayable builder. Missing storeys in an old spec is a validation failure to explain, not permission to reconstruct a design.
Scope: scripts/redo_here.py, lib/builds/feature_build.py, their existing tests, and the redo skill. Define reapply as rerunning the current recorded builder/spec without redesign; it is not guaranteed to reproduce historical blocks when inputs changed. Redo remains redesign from evidence. Exact historical replay is outside scope.
Acceptance: future feature_build applies record structured builder kind and world-relative spec path (or explicit absolute path) in existing journal metadata. Inspect other feature builder entry points before promising universal provenance; record supported script builders explicitly and report unsupported/legacy builders as unknown. redo_here exposes builder kind/path, provenance source and availability, preserving its existing script field for callers. Any legacy filename discovery is labelled inferred and never represented as recorded provenance; do not automatically execute an inferred command or arbitrary journal command text.
Resolve relative CLI spec paths against the explicit world's root and preserve absolute paths; document this rule and remove cwd dependence. Before any undo, validate the builder/spec exists and the current spec validates; a missing or invalid builder stops without clearing the feature. For valid reapply, follow undo-first and lock/readback/recovery requirements; do not silently pass --overwrite or edit/migrate an invalid spec. If rebuilding after a successful undo fails, report the remaining undone state and recovery route.
Verification: synthetic journal entries with recorded spec/script, legacy unknown/inferred builder, missing file, invalid spec and two cwd values resolving the same world-relative spec; absolute path compatibility; failure before undo leaves the build intact. Extend test_redo_here and test_feature_build; no world data or live apply.

tasks.title: Allow evidence-backed tree rooting on hard surfaces and one-block edge shunts
tasks.notes:
Accepted tree shunt plan: replace lawn-only/material allowlists with evidence-led rooting, following the revised decor approach. Concrete or other hard surface alone must not reject an evidenced tree; allow lawns, gravel, paved courtyards, plazas and pavements, including unresolved small planting pits. Trunks must not root in carriageway or water; apply that check to the trunk ground footprint, not the crown centre or canopy footprint. When an evidenced trunk falls on the edge of carriageway/water, allow at most one block of adjustment onto an immediately adjacent valid rooting position. Choose deterministically, keep the canopy aligned with the observed crown as closely as possible, and record the original position, adjusted position and reason. Never chain adjustments or move farther until a tree fits. If no valid position exists within one block, leave unplaced with a review reason. Canopies may overhang carriageway, water and neighbouring cells subject to existing collision, ownership and mask rules; #218 already permits leaf-only overhang into unprepared neighbours. Preserve feature-zone protection and trunk ownership within the planting cell; do not change ground merely to legalize a tree. Align foliage rules, planners/review images and reports; add synthetic tests for legal hard ground, successful one-block edge shunt, no legal neighbour, maximum distance, deterministic choice, blocked trunk and unaffected canopy overhang. Backlog only; not implemented.
Refinement 2026-10-31: target lib/layers/trees_layer.py plan_cell and the existing tree review/replan paths. Current code already grants some paved surfaces and feature-zone exceptions to aerial/mapped crowns; preserve those evidenced exceptions rather than accidentally tightening them. Identify which crown sources count as evidenced and keep detector/dense-fill policy unchanged. Evaluate carriageway/water using the existing semantic map and live surface checks; hard-surface material alone is neither evidence of a road nor proof of legal rooting. Missing surface/unknown water status must produce a review reason, not a guessed height.
For the edge adjustment, use a horizontal displacement of at most one block from the accepted pre-shunt trunk position: same position first, then the four orthogonally adjacent positions (no diagonals or chained search). Apply all trunk, cell-boundary, feature-zone/explicit exception, collision and mask checks to each candidate; never shift just to dodge a blocked trunk on otherwise legal ground. Choose the smallest displacement from the observed crown, with a documented stable coordinate tie-break. Keep this shunt separate from existing lidar/crown snapping and report both so successive stages cannot conceal movement. Extend existing plan/review artifacts with original/final trunk and reason; retain current readers. Synthetic acceptance includes cell-edge refusal and existing courtyard exceptions as well as the listed hard-ground/shunt/overhang cases.

tasks.title: Report missing provider packages clearly at affected CLI boundaries
tasks.notes:
Split from #220 during refinement 2026-10-31: missing-provider diagnostics are independent of running-world discovery. Related completed #202 fixed world activation/import timing; do not reopen or duplicate that fix without a failing case.
Problem: redo_here against a checkout without an expected world provider can still expose an import traceback. script_env.resolve_provider_package raises FileNotFoundError; world_provider.load_world_provider wraps missing package/module as ImportError, while run_world_provider already emits SystemExit. Trace the actual import path before choosing the catch boundary.
Acceptance: redo_here and affected equivalent CLI paths return nonzero with a concise message naming the selected world, missing package/module and local-provider configuration to inspect. Keep Python-library exceptions useful; convert only the known missing-provider condition at the appropriate CLI boundary. Never blanket-catch ImportError/FileNotFoundError, hide exceptions raised inside an existing provider, silently select another world, install a provider or change system/world resolution order. Discovery in #220 must work without providers regardless.
Verification: temporary synthetic world/package fixtures for missing package, missing module, a valid provider and an unrelated exception inside a provider that remains visible as a real bug. Extend existing provider/redo CLI tests without loading world-owned providers. No live server needed.

tasks.title: Reapply refusal for a missing builder gives the right recovery advice
tasks.notes: Found by running scripts/reapply_feature.py --world southampton-build houses_kitchener_road_w176648814 (dry run). It refuses correctly: 'no available recorded builder; refusing undo (legacy/inferred builders need review)'. But the message then says 'Inspect site_recover status for an interrupted write, or reconcile for drift', and ends 'undo completed=False'. Neither fits: nothing was interrupted and nothing drifted; the cause is a missing builder record, and no undo was attempted. Give each refusal reason its own advice: no recorded builder -> say the feature has no replayable builder and point to redo (redesign) as the way forward; invalid or missing spec -> name the spec problem; only a failure after a successful undo mentions undone state, site_recover and reconcile. Drop 'undo completed=False' when no undo ran. Add a test per reason in test_reapply_feature. Related to #225 (provenance); small enough to ship apart from it.
